description:
Hi! I’m Yaren, a student innovator from the Philippines, Flying solo. I'm tackling the climate adaptation challenge for farmers using NASA Earth data (SMAP, GPM, POWER).

I'm building an interactive web tool that turns complex satellite metrics into practical agricultural advice. I handle the product direction, UI prototyping, and storytelling. let's build something impactful!
summary:
AgroPulse is an interactive web-based climate advisory dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to help farmers proactively adapt to intensifying climate volatility. Built as an intuitive decision-support tool, AgroPulse translates complex satellite datasets—specifically NASA POWER (agroclimatology), SMAP (soil moisture), and GPM (precipitation)—into clear, localized, and actionable agricultural insights.

Farmers and local agricultural planners can select their specific region and crop type to instantly view real-time risk metrics, including soil moisture deficits, surface temperature extremes, and precipitation forecasts. Furthermore, AgroPulse features an interactive Climate Scenario Simulator that models shifting weather patterns (such as El Niño dry spells or heavy monsoons) and delivers immediate, practical adaptation strategies.

This solution is critical because smallholder farmers often lack access to timely, localized environmental intelligence. By democratizing NASA Earth data into a simple digital interface, AgroPulse empowers vulnerable agricultural communities to protect their yields, optimize resource management, and secure long-term food security in a changing climate.
details:
What AgroPulse Does & How It Works

AgroPulse is an interactive, browser-based agricultural climate advisory dashboard designed to help smallholder farmers and local agricultural planners make data-driven decisions in the face of climate volatility. By translating complex satellite Earth observation datasets—specifically NASA POWER (agroclimatology and solar irradiance), SMAP (surface and root-zone soil moisture), and GPM (precipitation forecasts)—into plain-language metrics, AgroPulse removes the technical barrier between orbital science and everyday farming.

Users select their specific agricultural region (such as Batangas, Nueva Ecija, or Bukidnon in the Philippines) and target crop (Rice, Corn, Coffee, or Vegetables) to view immediate environmental risk assessments, soil moisture deficits, and temperature alerts. Additionally, AgroPulse includes an interactive Climate Scenario Simulator that allows users to test extreme weather conditions—such as El Niño dry spells or heavy monsoon downpours—and immediately receive tailored, actionable crop adaptation recommendations.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Democratizing NASA Earth Data: Turns raw satellite telemetry into clear, localized advice that farmers can understand and apply without needing scientific training.
  • Proactive Yield Protection: Helps farmers anticipate drought stress, waterlogging, and heat spikes early, reducing crop loss and optimizing water and fertilizer usage.
  • Intended Impact: Strengthens climate resilience and long-term food security for vulnerable smallholder farming communities, starting with Philippine agricultural zones and scalable to rural regions worldwide.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Development & Architecture: Built as a lightweight, responsive web application using HTML5, Vanilla JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS (MIT License) for fast performance even on low-bandwidth connections.
  • Prototyping & Presentation Tools: Developed and tested using Google AI Studio, with collaborative workflow and code refinement assisted by Google Gemini, and pitch deck design structured via Gamma.
  • Assets & Licensing: Uses 100% original inline SVGs, public-domain NASA dataset references, and open-source libraries to ensure full compliance with open-source hackathon standards.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

  • Creativity: Instead of presenting farmers with intimidating scientific charts or raw satellite coordinates, AgroPulse blends a clean, accessible dashboard with an interactive "What-If" Climate Scenario Simulator—turning climate data into an intuitive, hands-on planning tool.
    • Accessibility & Low-Bandwidth Readiness: Engineered as a lightweight web tool so rural users with limited internet connectivity or basic devices can load advisories smoothly.
    • Hyper-Local Relevance: Tailored recommendations to specific regional microclimates and staple crops rather than generic, one-size-fits-all weather warnings.
    • Actionability Over Raw Numbers: Every satellite metric is paired directly with a practical farming step (e.g., mulching, adjusting irrigation schedules, or reinforcing drainage) so users know what to do, not just what the weather is.
